narrative:
Hello Drug Safety Team,

Ferncliff Medical is forwarding a report received from a physician assistant in the US. This is a spontaneous report and we have not been able to obtain further details yet.

The patient is a 59-year-old woman who takes metformin er 750 mg for type 2 diabetes mellitus. The physician assistant described two problems in this patient: muscle spasming, and a deficiency in vitamin B6. The reporter did not give us the start date of the metformin or the timing of either problem, and we do not know the exact duration. The reporter told us that both problems have since cleared up and the patient has recovered.

The physician assistant said they consider this a medically significant event for the patient. No other medications were mentioned as suspect, and we have no information on other medications the patient takes.

We will follow up with the reporter for onset dates, how long the patient had been taking metformin er, and any other relevant history. The reporter was friendly but said the clinic was busy that day, so the call was brief.

Please let us know if you need anything else in the meantime.

Kind regards,

Ben Fontaine, Drug Safety Associate, Ferncliff Medical

what_happened: the reporter assessed this event as medically significant

style_given.sign_off: Ben Fontaine, Drug Safety Associate, Ferncliff Medical

narrative:
Dear Drug Safety Team,

I am writing about a 31-year-old male patient who takes Sertraline Hcl 100 mg, one tablet each morning. He came to us complaining of pain in the upper abdomen and more general abdominal pain. Imaging then showed a cyst in the liver that had bled. He was admitted to hospital. I would regard this as a significant event for him. Start date and outcome are not known to me. Please contact me if you need more detail.

Kind regards,
Dmitri Thornton, pharmacist

narrative:
Dear Drug Safety Team,

I am a community pharmacist in Japan, and I am writing to report a case involving atorvastatin calcium.

One of my regular patients, whose age and sex I would rather not specify here, has been taking atorvastatin calcium. I do not have the dose, the start date or the indication to hand. The patient has now developed dementia. I cannot say how long ago this began, and I have not been able to establish whether any other factors are involved. As far as I am aware, no other medicines are under suspicion in this case.

I would consider this a medically significant event, given the impact on the patient and the family. I have no information yet on the current outcome, but I can try to find out more if that would help your assessment.

Apologies for the brevity. It has been a busy week at the pharmacy with the rainy season visitors. Please let me know what further details you need.

Kind regards,

Mei Thornton, pharmacist

what_happened: the reporter assessed this event as medically significant

narrative:
Subject matter forwarded from our French reporting channel, case received this week.

Hello Drug Safety team,

We are passing on a report from a doctor in France about a 31-year-old woman. The doctor told us she was prescribed Sertraline Hcl 50 mg once daily for mixed anxiety and depressive disorder, starting 21 July 2021. She was also put on chlorpromazine 25 mg once daily from the same date, for the same condition, and oxazepam, which began on 9 July 2021 (dose not provided). The doctor regards all three as possible suspects.

The doctor described the patient as developing a pregnancy-related blood pressure condition, which the doctor called pre-eclampsia. She was admitted to hospital because of it. The doctor reports that she has since recovered and the problem has resolved. No further details on her stay were given, and we do not have information on timing of onset relative to the drugs, or on any other treatments.

The doctor viewed the event as a significant one and wanted it reported. We can ask them for more information if you need it.

Kind regards,

Zofia Dubois, Drug Safety Associate, Quarry Hill Health

what_happened: the patient was admitted to hospital

narrative:
Hello,

We are forwarding a report received from a pharmacist in the US. She described a 74-year-old man who has been taking warfarin for atrial fibrillation since about 15 October 2020. The pharmacist said the patient has developed anaemia from low iron stores. She mentioned no other medicines. She did not give the dose, the date the anaemia was noticed, the treatment, or the current outcome, and we have not been able to confirm any of these. We can go back to her with follow-up questions if you need them.

Kind regards,
Carmen Brennan, Drug Safety Associate, Dunmore Pharma Services

narrative:
Hello, this is a message for the drug safety department. My name is Emeka Fontaine. I'm 77 years old, a woman, and yes, the name is a family one, so don't be confused. Sorry, there's a bit of noise, my neighbour is cutting the hedge and the rain has just stopped.

I take atorvastatin calcium, 20 milligrams, once a day. I started it around the 21st of November 2021. The doctor gave it to me for my high blood pressure. I'm not sure that is what it's usually used for, but that is what I was told it was for.

Anyway, I'm calling because my liver has been damaged. I'm not certain how it happened, only that it did, and I think it's connected to this tablet. It's getting better slowly. It isn't completely back to normal yet, but it's improving.

I'd say this is a significant matter, and I wanted it on record. The doctor seemed concerned too. I'm not taking anything else that I'd suspect.

Please call me back if you need more details. Thank you very much. Goodbye.

Emeka Fontaine

what_happened: the reporter assessed this event as medically significant

fidelity_additions.why: The doctor's concern is not in the facts; only the reporter's own assessment of medical significance is given.

narrative: Hi, this message is for the drug safety line. My name is Samir Ubaldi, and I'm calling about my wife. She's 34. She's been taking metformin ER 500 mg, I'm not sure exactly when she started, maybe a few weeks back, you'd have to ask her. Anyway, she had what looked like an allergic reaction to it. Her skin broke out in a rash, red and blotchy, and she was really reacting to something, which we figured was the pill since nothing else changed that we know of. I don't have the exact dates, sorry. The dog's barking in the background, ignore that. I just wanted to get this on record with you people. I can give you a call-back number, it's the one I'm calling from, so you should have it on your end. If someone could ring me back, that would be great. I'm usually free after five, since I'm at work till then. Thanks very much. Bye now.

narrative:
Dear Drug Safety Team,

I am writing to report a death in a patient of mine, a 74-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes who had been taking Metformin Hydrochloride 1500 mg daily since 2020. I do not have the exact dosing schedule beyond that.

She developed a build-up of lactate with a marked acid imbalance in the blood, which I believe was related to the metformin. Despite our efforts, she died. I would regard this as a very significant event, particularly as she had been stable on the treatment for several years.

I have no other suspect medications to report. I am happy to provide further details if you need them, though some information is not available to me at present.

Kind regards,
Dr Aidan Iwasaki

fidelity_additions.quote: particularly as she had been stable on the treatment for several years
fidelity_additions.why: The facts do not say the patient's diabetes or condition was stable on metformin. They give only the start year (2020).

narrative:
Hello, this is a message for the drug safety team. My name is Dmitri Iwasaki, I'm calling from the UK. Sorry, I've got the dog going mad in the background, bear with me.

I'm calling about my sister. She's 50 and has been taking sertraline, 50 milligrams once a day, since about the middle of August 2021. I'm not totally sure what it was prescribed for, something general, I don't think anyone put a precise name on it.

Anyway, her fingernails have these small dents, little pits all over the surface, like someone's pressed a pin into them. She's mentioned it a few times and it hasn't gone away. As far as I know it's still the same now.

I don't have the batch number or anything like that. I just wanted to report it properly. You can reach me on this number, I'm usually free after five once I'm done at work. Thanks very much. Bye.
